A write-ahead log is a file that documents every data change that is made to the database.
After a crash, the database is still available to read from, but it is not available to write to. At this point, the database can recover by replaying the log from the last checkpoint, which is a point where the log was flushed to disk. When a write operation is made to the database, it is first written to the write-ahead log. This means that the contents of the log are always available on disk. After each checkpoint, the contents of the log are also written to disk. When the database crashes, the contents of the log are still on disk, but the changes to the database itself are not. The database can recover from the crash by reading the contents of the log from disk and replaying it. Each log entry contains enough information to recreate the change that was originally made. The database can therefore use the log to recreate the changes that were not written to disk before the crash.
